- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Art Institute of Chicago has one of the largest and most renowned Impressionist collections in the world.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The collection includes works by Claude Monet, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Mary Cassatt, Edgar Degas, and Camille Pissarro.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Highlights of the Impressionist collection include:
  1. Monet's "Water Lilies" (1919) - a depiction of his garden at Giverny.
  2. Renoir's "Acrobat's Family with a Monkey" (1890) - a vibrant painting showcasing color and composition.
  3. Cassatt's "The Child's Bath" (1893) - a scene of a mother bathing her child.
  4. Degas's "Dancer at the Bar" (1888) - an example of capturing the beauty of the human form.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The museum regularly rotates its Impressionist collection.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Art Institute of Chicago offers daily guided tours, including ones focused on the Impressionist collection.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Guided tours are led by trained docents who provide in-depth information about the artworks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The museum offers a free mobile app that provides audio commentary for many artworks, including those in the Impressionist collection.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The museum provides self-guided tour brochures and interactive kiosks throughout the galleries.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The museum offers audio descriptions for visitors with visual impairments.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Art Institute of Chicago hosts lectures, workshops, and events focused on Impressionism and art history.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of events include lectures by art historians, gallery talks, workshops, and special events.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To find out about upcoming events, users can visit the museum's website, sign up for the newsletter, follow social media, and contact Visitor Services or the Education Department.
